skill.name: browser-testing-with-screenshots
skill.description: Automates Chrome browser testing with visual verification, element selection, page content checks, and screenshot capture for web UI workflows.
skill.summary: Automate Chrome UI testing with screenshots and DevTools-based browser helpers.
skill.author: AgentWorkforce

security_audit.summary: The skill is documentation-only, but it intentionally directs agents to control Chrome, capture screenshots, extract cookies and content, and run page JavaScript. Markdown-only backtick hits were dismissed, while browser session, screenshot, JavaScript evaluation, and third-party installation risks were confirmed.

remediation.issue: Default browser profile and cookie access can expose user sessions.
remediation.suggestion: Default to a fresh isolated profile, require explicit approval for preserved sessions, and remove cookie viewing from quick-reference examples.

remediation.issue: Screenshot workflows can capture secrets or private page content.
remediation.suggestion: Add clear guidance to use test accounts, redact sensitive areas, and avoid screenshots of production or personal pages.

remediation.issue: Page JavaScript evaluation can read or modify authenticated browser state.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer read-only checks, safely quote selectors, and require approval before mutating forms or clicking authenticated actions.

remediation.issue: Third-party browser tooling is installed from an unpinned repository.
remediation.suggestion: Pin a release or commit, document integrity verification, and avoid broad PATH installation without validation.

semantic_findings.title: Authenticated Browser Session Exposure
semantic_findings.description: The skill recommends preserving browser state and includes cookie access. DevTools-based automation against a personal profile can expose authenticated sessions.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The source explicitly references cookie listing, preserved user profiles, and using the default profile to keep login state. These are direct indicators of session exposure risk.

semantic_findings.title: Arbitrary Page JavaScript Execution
semantic_findings.description: The workflow runs JavaScript in the active page to set fields, click selected elements, and serialize form data. This can read or modify sensitive page state.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documented commands directly call browser-eval.js with page JavaScript, including form mutation and form data extraction. The behavior is explicit in the source.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned Third-Party Browser Tool Installation

content.value_statement: Visual UI checks are slow when teams must repeat browser steps manually. This skill guides Chrome-based testing with screenshots, element selection, and page checks.
actual_capabilities: Guides installation and verification of agent-tools browser commands.
Starts Chrome with DevTools Protocol access for interactive testing.
Navigates local web applications and waits for pages to load.
Captures screenshots for baseline, form, dashboard, and page evidence.
Uses interactive element picking to select buttons, fields, and menus.
Runs page JavaScript and extracts readable page content for checks.
limitations: Requires external agent-tools commands to be installed and available in PATH.
Depends on Chrome and a reachable DevTools Protocol port.
Screenshots, cookies, and page content can include sensitive user data.
Best suited for UI workflows, not API-only testing.

use_cases.title: Verify Local UI Changes
use_cases.description: Open a localhost app, capture screenshots, and confirm visible changes after a frontend update.

use_cases.title: Collect Test Evidence
use_cases.description: Run a browser flow and save screenshots that show login, dashboard, and profile states.

use_cases.title: Review Product Flows
use_cases.description: Navigate key screens and use screenshots to compare expected behavior with current UI output.

prompt_templates.title: Capture A Baseline
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner check for one local page.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use browser-testing-with-screenshots to open my localhost page at [URL]. Capture a baseline screenshot and summarize visible layout issues.

prompt_templates.title: Check A Login Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Test the login flow for [URL] with a test account. Capture screenshots before and after submit, then report visible success or error states.

prompt_templates.title: Verify Dynamic Content
prompt_templates.prompt: Open [URL], wait for dynamic content, select the main navigation, and verify that expected dashboard text appears on screen.

prompt_templates.title: Document A Multi Page Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a visual test across login, dashboard, and profile pages. Save screenshots, note each page state, and list any visual regressions.

output_examples.input: Open the dashboard and capture a screenshot after the data loads.
output_examples.output: The dashboard loaded after a short wait. A screenshot was saved, and the summary notes visible navigation, charts, and empty-state warnings.

output_examples.input: Test the login form with a test user and confirm the result.
output_examples.output: The form accepted the test credentials and moved to the dashboard. Screenshots show the initial form, filled form, and final dashboard.

output_examples.input: Check three local pages for visual regressions.
output_examples.output: Screenshots were captured for login, dashboard, and profile. The report flags one spacing issue on the profile page.

best_practices: Use test accounts and non-sensitive local data for screenshot workflows.
Start with a fresh browser profile when session state is not required.
Wait for page load or specific elements before capturing screenshots.
anti_patterns: Do not capture screenshots of production pages that contain private data.
Do not preserve a personal browser profile unless the user approves it.
Do not use browser JavaScript evaluation for unrelated page changes.

faq.question: What browser does this skill use?
faq.answer: It is written for Chrome with DevTools Protocol access through external browser helper commands.

faq.question: Can it test localhost applications?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples focus on local development URLs and visual checks during implementation.

faq.question: Does it replace a full test framework?
faq.answer: No. It supports visual checks and evidence capture, but it does not provide full test orchestration.

faq.question: Can screenshots expose sensitive data?
faq.answer: Yes. Use test accounts, fresh profiles, and redaction when pages may show private information.

faq.question: Does it require extra tools?
faq.answer: Yes. It requires agent-tools browser commands to be installed and available in PATH.

faq.question: Can it inspect page content?
faq.answer: Yes. It can extract readable content and run page JavaScript through the browser helper tools.
